lxc_269d3e1855ff301f.text: Cricket has two teams, a ball, and a bat.

lxc_02f46ff2c65978c7.text: Teams score runs and try to get batters out.

lxc_d7007092c15e4805.text: This simple guide explains cricket for beginners.

lxc_5c81b3a9ebf19049.text: A cricket match has two teams.

lxc_5fcf9648bfa1b8d0.text: The main action happens on the pitch.

lxc_eea18feabe982554.text: It is a long area in the centre.

lxc_d8050bbf2ddc8dfe.text: There is one wicket at each end of the pitch.

lxc_a0623efd6fd3c198.text: A wicket has three wooden sticks.

lxc_bce12850183fd598.text: Two small wooden pieces sit on top.

lxc_272d193265855fb5.text: The wickets are important targets in the game.

lxc_02fb8ef41beb9a5c.text: The batter tries to hit the ball and score runs.

lxc_34b8e14e4b2ec8db.text: Two batters are on the pitch.

lxc_53cecb0933881eaf.text: The bowler bowls the ball toward the batter and wicket.

lxc_18cef490ab674bc0.text: The bowler tries to stop runs or get the batter out.

lxc_29c69096f5abde00.text: The wicketkeeper stands behind the wicket.

lxc_cc92bd943a75f600.text: This player catches or stops the ball.

lxc_7d0c27f1f264ac67.text: They catch the ball, stop it, and throw it back.

lxc_1ee9530c72ad8f38.text: Runs are the points in cricket.

lxc_1ce1e1ba3188a10a.text: For one run, the two batters run and safely change ends.

lxc_8ada9f78fa03d062.text: A batter can also score a boundary.

lxc_ee2815b33a58fa2b.text: The edge of the field is the boundary.

lxc_21d67cb54b0e74e7.text: A ball that reaches it after touching the ground scores four runs.

lxc_08e4603510512eef.text: A ball that goes over it without touching the ground scores six runs.

lxc_7ac076899a2fca42.text: Team Blue scores one run, then four, then six.

lxc_e431f2e4c9afec30.text: This means eleven runs and no batters out.

lxc_261e95a20de3b6e2.text: The bowler does not bowl forever.

lxc_69182650eb2ad0d7.text: Cricket divides the bowling into short groups.

lxc_1ad1928c24414629.text: One group is called an over.

lxc_8c9e435052141ef9.text: An over has six valid balls.

lxc_88a20b47c87ef724.text: A valid ball is a delivery that counts in the game.

lxc_5aeb8690387a3044.text: The bowler bowls the first valid ball.

lxc_d7cc6e96c0ea0aec.text: This continues until the sixth valid ball.

lxc_d8d244b6b18b8229.text: Overs help players count the game.

lxc_55e0da5f295687f9.text: For example, three complete overs contain eighteen valid balls.

lxc_9308946093de34c5.text: When a batter is out, that batter’s turn ends.

lxc_1e4bd7d4c265fe0f.text: Another batter usually comes to the pitch.

lxc_3e90ce07203fa75a.text: There are several ways to get a batter out.

lxc_717b5e26f010a2c8.text: Bowled: The bowler’s ball hits and breaks the wicket.

lxc_08de5c2263547f45.text: Caught: The batter hits the ball.

lxc_5554a674d5001cd1.text: A fielder catches it before it touches the ground.

lxc_237f36ff7feccc8e.text: Run out: A batter is outside the safe area near the wicket.

lxc_8eef99e24ff2d872.text: A fielder uses the ball to break that wicket fairly.

lxc_a38fde4dac1f4c9b.text: Cricket has three main international formats.

lxc_7a5386a5c2ff277e.text: An innings is one team’s turn to bat.

lxc_6678fa5d93f07ad7.text: A Test match can last five days.

lxc_542d91baf3cbb61e.text: Each team can have two innings.

lxc_966aa30248b56698.text: Test cricket is the longest format.

lxc_f78870f94ef523a5.text: An ODI is a One Day International.

lxc_4b740b64e5a353fa.text: A T20 International has 20 overs for each team.

lxc_e02f47bee03da8ce.text: It usually takes about three hours.

lxc_82e4733992a8212e.text: It is the shortest of these three formats.

lxc_4e904fd157194a67.text: The basic ideas stay the same.

lxc_9e4f953d64f21f8f.text: Teams bat, bowl, field, score runs, and get batters out.
